值得閱讀的理由

  • 揭露市面上隨身 Wi-Fi 宣稱「超低價、超大流量」背後的限速與虛標陷阱。
  • 實測從不到 30 元到高達 2,199 元的多款設備，提供真實極限環境下的網速與延遲表現。
  • 詳細解析第三方流量商與官方服務的差異，幫助消費者在選購時避免資安風險與消費爭議。

摘要

隨身 Wi-Fi 的宣傳話術與極限場景實測

作者從各大網購平台購入了多款熱銷隨身 Wi-Fi，甚至包含一台要價 2,199 元的高階旗艦，藉此驗證商家標榜的「極速訊號」與「超便宜大流量」套餐是否屬實。作者首先在空曠公園進行網速測試，各家表現平平，僅中興展現出約 37.5 MB/s 的水準；隨後將所有設備帶至網路環境極為嚴苛的深圳北站進行極限測試，結果原本領先的中興幾乎斷網，僅華為能勉強維持微弱連線，證明宣傳效果與現實體驗落差極大。

低價隨身 Wi-Fi 的陷阱與離譜後台

作者實測了在美團以不到 30 元購得的超低價設備，點出硬體只是門票、後續加值方案才是暴利所在的產業現狀。此類方案存在階梯式分速，即便加購 109 元的頂級不限速套餐，在消耗約 100GB 後仍會遭遇斷崖式限速或斷線。此外，該設備使用可能具安全隱憂的舊式可拆鋰電池，後台管理機制更是離譜——只需掃描機身二維碼即可在遠端修改 Wi-Fi 密碼，且各項設定指令需要漫長等待且無法多工執行，資安與操作體驗堪憂。

第三方流量商套路與無電池直插設備表現

接著評測售價 339 元的華為 Mobile WiFi 3 Pro，作者發現第三方通路常搭配名為「華粉物聯」的非官方 SIM 卡，這類第三方卡號常有嚴重虛標與惡意限速，例如宣稱 3000GB 的方案在用完 10GB 後即被降速至 2 MB/s。隨後登場的《王者榮耀》聯名款設備主打無電池、手機供電直插，雖宣稱能降低遊戲延遲，但實測延遲高達 70 至 110 ms，且其流量設有單日 50GB 上限且不累計，使用過程還伴隨頻繁斷線需重新插拔的問題。

高價中興 U60 Pro 旗艦實測與多功能探索

最後測試要價 2,190 元的中興 U60 Pro，其做工精良，配備螢幕、10,000 mAh 電池與 18W 充電，但在長時間放於口袋使用時發熱明顯。作者監控其流量消耗，發現設備端顯示的數值與後台存在誤差，但最終實際使用量確實達到近 1500GB 標稱額度。該機型支援Android 專用 NFC 觸碰連網、境外漫遊卡儲值以及插自有實體 SIM 卡作為外接網卡或收發簡訊等多種進階功能，表現全面但入手門檻相對高昂。

================================================

I also picked up the priciest portable Wi‑Fi unit,. priced at 2199 yuan,. to see if it can outperform all the others. Every seller claims blazing-fast speeds. and rock-solid signals. Their data plans sound outrageous too:. 900GB for 39 yuan,. 1500GB for 29.8 yuan. This one takes the cake. 3000GB for just 9.9 yuan. It's almost like the three major telecom operators. have to buy data from you. If these portable Wi‑Fi devices are fast. and such great value,. is there even a need for wired broadband? Alright, before we dive into the main review,. let's test their network speeds. In an open area like a park,. all of them are barely usable. ZTE pulled far ahead,. hitting roughly 37.5 MB/s. The outdoor park didn't push them hard enough,. so I brought all these portable Wi‑Fis straight. to Shenzhen North Station. Network conditions here. are absolute hell. But reality hits hard. Even ZTE, our winner from the last round,. couldn't handle Shenzhen North Station. Its speed was practically the same as being offline. Surprisingly, Huawei. managed to crawl along, just barely. Wow. So the real-world experience of portable Wi‑Fi. is nothing like the marketing. Now let's go through each device one by one. First up, this one I got on Meituan. for less than 30 yuan. For those who don't know:. the portable Wi‑Fi hardware itself is just a ticket to get started. The real expense comes from. the data plans you top up later. Take this device for example. The 69-yuan package is medium-speed single-channel,. while the 79-yuan plan. is the premium high-speed multi-channel option. And that's not the top tier. You can pay 109 yuan for.

a month of unlimited data. with a claimed 200% speed boost. Sounds like speeds would go through the roof! But here's the thing:. I subscribed to this exact plan. during our earlier speed test,. and the performance. was terrible. With this unlimited data package,. everything worked fine at first,. averaging around. 3 MB/s. But once I used roughly 100GB,. the speed dropped to zero. It came back after a while. I can't tell if this is just unstable connectivity. or some kind of PWM-style throttling. The worst part is. there's no fixed trigger time. You could be in the middle of an online game team fight,. and then lose connection instantly. Talk about tilting hard. Inside the box, besides the main unit,. there's a separate battery. I haven't seen this type of lithium battery in ages. My first thought was grabbing a universal charger to juice it up. Just as I was about to place an order,. I noticed a warning on the product page:. do not use universal chargers for this portable Wi‑Fi battery. Huh? Feels like they're calling me out. I looked it up,. and the issue is insufficient voltage. Even if you force it to charge,. it won't fully power the battery, charges slowly,. and may even cause an explosion. As many of you know,. normally to configure a router,. you connect to it first. and log into the backend web portal. But for this model,. you scan the QR code on the back to adjust settings. you don't even need to connect to its Wi‑Fi. I sent this QR code to. a friend in Dongguan,. and he actually managed to change my Wi‑Fi password. That's absolutely ridiculous. At this point, some sharp viewers might say:. "Well, just change the password back, right?" Yeah, but with this type of portable Wi‑Fi,. you have to wait for every operation. Changing the Wi‑Fi password takes 5 minutes,. and renaming the network also takes 5 minutes. It doesn't support multi-tasking. If you want to rename the network after changing the password,. you have to wait until the password update finishes first. What even is this? Are we still in 2026?

Our second contender today is. the Huawei Mobile WiFi 3 Pro,. priced at 339 yuan,. making it the second most expensive portable Wi‑Fi in our test. Since it's a Huawei device,. it integrates with the Huawei ecosystem. The app packs plenty of function entries. except for data top-ups. To recharge your data,. you need to pry open the back cover,. take out the battery,. and scan a QR code. It was during the top-up process that I found out:. the SIM card inside this unit. I bought from a third-party JD store. isn't an official Huawei SIM. It's from a provider called Huafen IoT. Huafen…. Huawei fans are called Huafen,. right? Wait a minute,. that's supposed to be Huawei Fans. So I dug deep into. Huafen IoT. Turns out. I'm far from the only one scammed. Lots of users are filing complaints. about falsified data allowances and speed throttling. It's absolutely outrageous. I checked their plans:. 3000GB for 89 yuan,. which averages. roughly 33.7GB per yuan. Sounds pretty decent, doesn't it? But what if I tell you. throttling kicks in after you use just 10GB? Yep. Right after I bought the plan. and burned through 10GB,. my speed got capped at 2 MB/s. Imagine. how long it would take. to get through 3000GB at only 2 MB/s. 华为官方的网络服务。Huawei's official network service is called Skyroam. When shopping,. make sure you double-check with customer support. Next up is our most unique contender. Look at it. It has no built-in battery. and requires constant power to run. At first glance, it sounds a bit useless. But plug it into your phone. hey, look at this:. Ethernet tethering. Your phone stays online. while broadcasting Wi‑Fi for others to use. The downside is. your phone battery.

drains a bit faster. The unit I have here is. a "Honor of Kings" co-branded edition. The product page claims. it drastically cuts latency. for smooth gaming,. to help you dominate matches. Time to fire up a TIMI game and test it out. In wired mode,. latency hovers around 70 ms,. sometimes spiking up to 110 ms. That latency and stability. are hardly"smooth gaming". The data plans aren't too pricey. For the tri-network plan,. the cheapest option is 1500GB per month. for just 49 yuan. Flymodem's data plan has a catch:. a daily cap of 50GB,. adding up to 1500GB over 30 days. Unused data does not roll over. If you use less one day, you lose that 50GB completely. There wasn't much persistent speed throttling during regular use,. but it kept randomly dropping connection. I had to unplug and re-plug the portable Wi‑Fi every time to restore service. You already put a daily cap on my data,. can't you at least let me use it without disconnections? The user experience is pretty bad. Our next device. probably left a strong impression. on you earlier. That's right, this is the most expensive portable Wi‑Fi in the whole lineup. the ZTE U60 Pro,. priced at 2190 yuan. This is my first time buying such a pricey portable Wi‑Fi. As they say, you get what you pay for. Its build quality is on a completely different level from the others. Look at this. It even comes with a built-in screen. You can adjust all settings right here. Besides the usual Wi‑Fi name and password options,. it supports multi-band integration. and lets you blacklist other people's devices. Pretty much all configuration options are available,. except for data top-ups. A screen alone. definitely doesn't justify a 2000-yuan price tag. Check out its thickness; it houses a 10,000 mAh battery. The USB‑C port supports charging up to 18W. Alright, even with the battery, it still shouldn't cost 2000 yuan. And even though it's rated for 18W,. it won't sustain that power continuously. When I leave the Wi‑Fi on in my pocket,. it gets scorching hot in no time. The device is costly,. and so is its data plan:. 1500GB for 79 yuan,.

which works out to only around 18.9GB per yuan. One great feature of the ZTE unit is that. it displays real-time data usage on the device. During my test,. I jotted down readings at regular intervals. and put together this table. You can easily see that. for the first roughly 100GB,. the usage shown on the device. was lower than what the website displayed. Starting at 200GB,. the figure on the device. overtook the website reading. I watched the gap. between these two numbers. keep growing: from 10.9%. to 11.3%,. then to 14.2%. By the time the data ran out,. the discrepancy hit 16.3%. That's absolutely wild. You might think I'm about to say. this portable Wi‑Fi. has severely inflated data claims. Actually, no. The website showed I used roughly 1440GB. Factoring in all kinds of measurement errors,. my real consumption was. indeed about 1500GB. But the device backend recorded 1675GB of usage. Hmm. Did it intentionally let me. use up the full 1500GB? Or did the backend forget to. cut my connection once I hit the 1500GB cap? There's an NFC logo right here. on the device. Just tap it to connect to the Wi‑Fi directly. But this function. Only Android Can Do. Phone users have no choice but to scan the QR code to connect. There's more. It even has a SIM card slot. with a pre-installed SIM. This card is meant for overseas travel. You can purchase data packages for different countries. through their official WeChat account. After purchase, the data gets loaded onto this SIM. Bring this abroad,. and you get both a power bank and internet access. Sounds perfect. But the rates? My wallet will probably run empty before my data does. If you don't want to. buy their data packages after purchasing this portable Wi‑Fi,. you can insert. your own SIM card into the slot,. and it will use the data from your SIM.

It can even receive. incoming text messages normally. Too bad though. us iPhone Air users don't have physical SIM cards. Alright,. time for our final contender today. We could understand. seeing ZTE and Huawei earlier,. after all, they genuinely run communications businesses. But. how did "this" end up here? Does Legion even have this product line? The device itself only costs 46.9 yuan. The design. screams Legion. Its back cover is removable. But once you take it apart, there's no battery inside. Just two words:. Top Up. It comes with. a slip of paper. stating. the device does not support fast charging. I took a closer look:. 5V1A. It's 2026 now. Where am I even supposed to find a 5V 1A charger? There must be a reason. for this requirement. The lowest-rated charger I own is already 66W. Oh wait,. I also have an 18W power bank; I almost forgot about it. And that's not all. Its data plan sounds insane:. 3000GB for just 9.9 yuan. I opened the data top-up page. Where's that promised 9.9-yuan 3000GB plan? Are they hiding fine print? The product page. doesn't mention data pricing at all. Where else could it be? Okay,. there are ten images in total. The first nine all look similar. Buried on the last one:. introductory top-up offer, 3000GB for 9.9 yuan,. valid for only three days. This merchant is really tricky. For regular purchases,. 1500GB costs 69 yuan. and 3000GB is 79 yuan. This data plan works the same way as Flymodem's:. daily data cap, unused data does not roll over. But Flymodem's data tracking is accurate. It shows nearly exactly how much you consume,. with very small discrepancies. For this Legion model,.

I bought the 1500GB package,. meaning. I get 50GB per day. Yet for two days in a row,. after only using roughly 40GB,. it warned me that my data was exhausted. The discrepancy hit 42.8%. On the third day, the gap shrank. I used 51GB. and the difference dropped to around 8%. Is this my fault,. or the device's? Just today,. I logged into the backend. It said I used 26GB on the 22nd. Wait a second. that was a Saturday, my day off. Who consumed those 26GB? My studio teammates. have been borrowing these portable Wi‑Fi units a lot lately. Some took them back to their hometowns,. others use them during commutes. One teammate. wanted to take one home. so he wouldn't have to fight for bandwidth with his family. Right after saying that,. he borrowed my most expensive portable Wi‑Fi. The next day he sent me just one word:. Awesome. I couldn't stop laughing. I even heard about a friend of a friend. who doesn't have wired broadband at home. He uses a portable Wi‑Fi as his home router. to supply internet for all household devices. Has anyone. watching tried anything more ridiculous than that? There are still plenty of pitfalls with portable Wi‑Fi. Don't just buy one on impulse. The good news is. these traps aren't impossible to spot. When browsing product pages,. don't only look at advertised speeds. Check carefully whether it is 4G or 5G,. Wi‑Fi 6 or Wi‑Fi 7. We want a solid experience. without wasting money. Don't blindly trust those seemingly unbeatable data packages. shown in preview images. Always ask customer service. for the official price list. and shop around. Compare value for money. Lastly, pick brands with reliable after-sales support. and stay away from white-label OEM products. OK, that wraps up everything for this video. If this video helped you,. remember to hit like, subscribe and ring the bell. It means a lot to me.

I'm Cherry. See you next time. Bye!
